Candidate overlap, in quote changes

Correlations of positive conventional package exposures over common dates in each series' last 252 observations. Invert the sign when only one trade direction is reversed. These are relationships between the expressions, not between their strategy returns or a recommended allocation.

Exact timing rule and interpretation

Original baseline: 504-observation fit, recalculated every five observations with prior data only. Alert at |z| ≥ 1.5 and < 3.5; fill at the next observed close.

Confirmed entry: freeze the fit and direction at that alert. On a later observation, require both a favourable package change over the previous three observations and a residual recovery of at least 0.25 training sigma from the worst signed residual since the alert. Expire after ten observations or fourteen calendar days. Cancel if the residual reaches the convergence/adverse boundary or the next data gap exceeds five calendar days. Fill at the next close.

Both exit on residual convergence through 0.25, adverse residual 3.5, or the holding limit of 40 observations/about 65 calendar days. Model coefficients and scale are frozen within an alert/trade; conditioned fair values move with the conditioning rates. Each variant maintains its own positions and cooldowns. Displayed target/stop levels map those residual rules to current conditioning rates; they are neither fixed P&L barriers nor forecasts.

The primary calculation uses actual package quote moves. Synthetic annual-pay, single-curve aging is a separate approximation, including simplified floating accrual. Carry is a hypothetical 40-calendar-day unchanged-curve calculation for a newly entered expression, not forecast return or carry remaining in the existing position. INR remains on the user-confirmed annual market quote convention.

All six candidates were selected from already inspected history. This is exploratory research. No significance claim, fresh holdout, backtested selected portfolio, live trade or forward-start substitution is implied.
